prompt: Read the image file {path}. It is a crop of one column of a printed 1854 Hebrew-English lexicon (Gesenius, Robinson translation). Transcribe every complete printed text line exactly, one array element per printed line, top to bottom. Preserve spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, printed abbreviations, section marks and end-of-line hyphenation. Hebrew, Aramaic, Arabic, Syriac, Greek and Ethiopic must be Unicode text with every visible vowel point, dagesh, accent and diacritic, written in logical order with no bidi control characters; keep the words of a right-to-left phrase in the order they are read, and keep the printed left-to-right order of separate items in a list. Where a page or column header, page number or catchword is present, include it as its own line. If a line is only partially visible at the top or bottom edge, omit it entirely rather than guessing. Never add, reorder, translate, normalise or omit anything that is fully visible. If the crop contains no text, return an empty array.

lines: שָׁלַל
1. to draw or pull out, sc. stalks of
grain from the handfuls, Ruth 2, 16.
Arab. سَلَّ id. Kindr. are Aram. שְׁלָא,
ܫܠܐ, Heb. נָשַׁל, שָׁלַף.
2. to strip off, to despoil, to spoil, to
plunder; rarely in the Aram. dialects,
as Chald. part. שׁוֹלֵל, Nasor. ࡔࡋࡋ, to
spoil.—Constr. c. acc. of thing, Ez. 26,
12; or of the person plundered 39, 10.
Hab. 2, 8. Zech. 2, 12. שָׁלַל שָׁלָל to spoil
the spoil, to seize the spoil, Is. 10, 6. Ez.
Niph. here some refer fut. יִשַּׁל Deut.
28, 40; but see in r. נָשַׁל.
Hithpo. אֶשְׁתּוֹלֵל Aram. for הִשְׁתּוֹלֵל to
be spoiled, plundered, Is. 59, 15.
Deriv. שׁוֹלָל and
שָׁלָל m. constr. שְׁלַל. 1. spoil, plun-
der, booty; Is. 33, 23 עַד שָׁלָל a prey of
spoil, from which connection of the
words it appears that עַד is the more
general word, and שָׁלָל the more spe-
cial; yet the latter is often general,
prey, booty, Gen. 49, 27. Num. 31, 11.
13. al. also of flocks and herds driven
off, 1 Sam. 15, 19. 21. שְׁלַל דָּוִד David's
spoil, driven off by him, 1 Sam. 30, 20;
but שְׁלַל אֹיְבֶיךָ the spoil of thine enemies,
taken from them, Deut. 20, 14. Josh. 22,
8. 1 Sam. 14, 30. To seize or take the
spoil is שָׁלַל שָׁלָל see the root no. 2;
הֵבִיא שׁ׳ to bring the spoil 2 Sam. 3, 22.
נָשָׂא שָׁלָל 2 Chr. 14, 12. Contra, חִלֵּק שָׁלָל
to divide the spoil, to distribute the boo-
Ps. 68, 13. al. Jer. 21, 9 and his life shall
be unto him for a booty, i. e. he shall be
preserved alive; and so 38, 2. 39, 18.
45, 5.—In the difficult passage Judg. 5,
30, צֶבַע רִקְמָתַיִם לְצַוְּארֵי שָׁלָל a dyed gar-
ment, two vestments of divers colours, for
the neck of the spoil, there is no good
meaning. Hence Gesenius and others
take שָׁלָל for אִישׁ שָׁלָל a spoiler, and
render: for the neck of the spoiler, i. e.
Sisera or any warrior; so Syr. Schnur-
rer, Rosenmueller, etc. Others, as De
Sacy, Studer, read לְצַוָּארָיו שָׁלָל, a spoil
for his neck, sc. Sisera's; and so Sept.
τῷ τραχήλῳ αὐτοῦ σκῦλα. Boettcher, in
שָׂלַם
Spicileg. p. 21, proposes to read לְצַוְּארֵי
שָׁלָל, a spoil for my neck, as the wish
of a woman expecting a portion of the
spoil. This perh. is best.
2. gain sc. by labour, profit, Germ.
Ausbeute, Prov. 31, 11. So Arab. غُنْمٌ
prey and gain; comp. Gr. ληΐζεσθαι to
plunder, also genr. to get, to gain.
* שָׁלֵם or שָׁלַם fut. יִשְׁלַם 1. to be
whole, entire, integer; hence
a) to be sound, safe, secure; Arab.
سَلِمَ, Syr. ܫܠܶܡ, id. Kindr. are r.
שָׁלָה, שָׁלַו. Job 9, 4 who hath set himself
against him, וַיִּשְׁלָם and been secure, in
safety. 22, 21.
b) to be completed, finished, ended;
e. g. the temple, 1 K. 7, 51; the walls
of the city, Neh. 6, 15; also of a period
of time, Is. 60, 20. Chald. שְׁלִם q. v.
Syr. ܫܠܶܡ id.
3. Denom. from שָׁלוֹם, to be at peace,
in friendship with any one. Part. c.
suff. שֹׁלְמִי Ps. 7, 5 my friend, ally, i. q.
אִישׁ שְׁלוֹמִי Ps. 41, 10. Part. pass. שָׁלוֹם
pacified, peaceful, 1 Sam. 20, 19. See
Pu. no. 2. Syr. ܫܠܶܡ c. ܠ, to consent,
to accord.
Piel שִׁלֵּם, 3 pl. in pause שִׁלֵּמוּ, to
make whole, entire, integrum fecit, viz.
a) to make secure, safe, c. acc. of
thing, Job 8, 6.
b) to complete, to finish, e. g. the tem-
ple, 1 K. 9, 25; comp. Kal no. 1. b.
c) to make whole, to make good; e. g.
to restore a thing lost Joel 2, 25, or stolen
Ez. 33, 15; to repay a debt 2 K. 4, 7. Ps.
d) to pay, to perform, to render, c. acc.
of thing, e. g. vows 2 Sam. 15, 7. Is. 19,
22, 27 ; praise as sacrifice, Hos. 14, 3 [2],
see in art. פַּר, comp. Ps. 56, 13. Trop.
to render or impart comfort, Is. 57, 18.
e) to requite, to recompense, to re-
ward, sc. like for like, both good 1 Sam.
24, 20. Ruth 2, 12, and also evil Gen. 44,
4 ; with לְ of pers. Deut. 7, 10. 32, 41.
thing, Is. 65, 6. Jer. 16, 18. 32, 18 ; with
לְ of pers. and acc. of thing, as שִׁלֵּם גְּמוּל
לְ see in גְּמוּל no. 1, שִׁלֵּם פֹּעַל לְ Job 34, 11.
